zh.title: 太空中心島脈探空火箭成功發射完成通訊驗證
zh.summary: 太空中心島脈火箭於屏東成功發射，完成全程通訊與各次系統飛行驗證。
body: 台灣國家太空中心（TASA）自主研製的首支探空火箭「島脈」（MARAHO）於2026年8月22日清晨在屏東旭海科研火箭發射場域成功執行首次飛試任務。此次發射順利完成了火箭點火、飛行及降落傘展開等關鍵發射作業，並成功進行了全程通訊等關鍵驗證，標誌著太空中心在入軌火箭計畫上取得重要進展。
根據國家太空中心的數據，探空火箭於當天上午7時10分點火升空。在點火後，火箭持續推進了18秒，起飛時的推力達到1500公斤重，最高速度達到每秒408公尺（相當於超音速的1.2馬赫）。火箭在起飛後第49秒順利抵達8.1公里的最高高度，整趟任務的總飛行時間為432秒，各項飛行程序均依規劃順利完成。
此次飛試的核心關鍵目標在於建立地面與火箭之間的全程通訊系統，以即時接收火箭於飛行過程中所下傳的觀測資料。在飛行末段，火箭依程序展開了兩階段降落傘並順利落海。儘管後續因海上風浪過高以及箭體持續漂移，導致回收團隊最終未能成功將箭體打撈上岸，但由於所有必要的飛行資料均已在飛行期間即時回傳，因此這並未影響主要飛試驗證數據的取得。
這款命名為「島脈」的探空火箭，其名稱取自台灣特有種且有「國蝶」之稱的寬尾鳳蝶，箭體外觀視覺設計亦融入其代表性的寬大紅色尾突。在規格方面，箭體總長為7.2公尺，直徑為0.4公尺，其推進系統採用了由90%雙氧水與聚丙烯（PP）組成的混合式推進劑。
國家太空中心自2023年在國家科學及技術委員會（國科會）的指導下啟動了入軌火箭計畫，終極目標是於2034年掌握自主入軌能力。為逐步降低大型載具開發風險，太空中心規劃於2029年以第一代次軌道測試火箭（STV1）驗證各項次系統，並於2031年透過第二代次軌道測試火箭（STV2）驗證完整載具，最終在2034年執行第一代入軌火箭飛試，預計將200公斤級酬載送入低地球軌道。

en.title: TASA Successfully Launches First Self-Developed Sounding Rocket MARAHO
en.summary: TASA successfully launches its first self-developed sounding rocket MARAHO in Pingtung for system verification.
body: Taiwan's National Space Agency (TASA) successfully launched its first self-developed sounding rocket, named "MARAHO," on the morning of August 22, 2026, from the Xuhai research rocket launch site in Pingtung. The successful test flight marked a major milestone for TASA's orbital rocket program, completing critical launch procedures including ignition, flight, parachute deployment, and establishing full end-to-end communication.

According to official flight parameters, the "MARAHO" rocket lifted off at 7:10 AM. The hybrid propulsion system fired for 18 seconds, generating a liftoff thrust of 1,500 kilograms. The rocket accelerated to a maximum speed of 408 meters per second, equivalent to supersonic speed at Mach 1.2. It reached its peak altitude of 8.1 kilometers 49 seconds after launch, completing a total flight duration of 432 seconds.

A primary objective of the mission was to test and verify the ground-to-rocket end-to-end communication system to enable real-time telemetry downlink during the flight. At the final stage of the flight, the rocket deployed its two-stage parachute system and landed in the ocean as planned. While high waves and drifting prevented the recovery team from retrieving the physical rocket body, TASA confirmed that all critical flight data had been successfully transmitted to the ground station during the flight, ensuring no impact on the test results.

The "MARAHO" rocket, named after Taiwan's endemic Agehana maraho butterfly, is 7.2 meters long with a diameter of 0.4 meters. Its propulsion system relies on a hybrid design utilizing 90% hydrogen peroxide and polypropylene (PP). The butterfly's prominent red tail protrusion inspired the visual design of the rocket, symbolizing the tail flames of a rocket during liftoff.

TASA initiated its domestic orbital rocket development project in 2023 under the guidance of the National Science and Technology Council. The agency aims to build sovereign space launch capabilities, with the long-term goal of sending a 200-kilogram payload into low Earth orbit by 2034. To mitigate development risks, TASA plans to launch the first-generation suborbital test rocket (STV1) in 2029 and the second-generation test rocket (STV2) in 2031 before the final orbital flight test.

zh.title: 達美航空班機驚現偽造WiFi網路 配合FAA及聯邦執法單位展開調查
zh.summary: 達美航空客機出現未授權WiFi；機組員暫停網路服務；執法單位與FAA介入調查
body: 達美航空（Delta Air Lines）8月10日由拉斯維加斯飛往亞特蘭大的DL591航班上，發現名為「Delta Wifi Fast」的未授權無線網路。達美航空澄清該網路非由公司提供或運作。
作為預防措施，機組人員暫停了該架波音（Boeing）757客機的乘客WiFi服務約30分鐘。達美航空強調公司系統未遭入侵，班機安全未受影響，目前正與聯邦執法部門及美國聯邦航空總署（FAA）展開調查。
網路安全公司 Cyviation 執行長 Eliran Almog 表示，該事件符合網路安全領域常見的「惡魔雙胞胎」攻擊手法，意圖透過偽造網路名稱誘騙乘客輸入帳密與個人資料。

en.title: Unauthorized WiFi Detected on Delta Flight DL591 Prompting FAA Investigation
en.summary: Delta Flight DL591 detected unauthorized WiFi onboard, prompting crew action and investigation by federal authorities.
body: On August 10, 2026, an unauthorized wireless network named "Delta Wifi Fast" was detected aboard Delta Air Lines Flight DL591 traveling from Las Vegas to Atlanta. Delta confirmed that the network was neither operated nor provided by the airline.

As a precautionary measure, the flight crew temporarily disabled the Boeing 757 passenger WiFi for approximately 30 minutes. Delta stated that its internal systems were not compromised, and the safety of the flight was never in question. The carrier is investigating the occurrence alongside federal law enforcement agencies and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

Cyviation CEO Eliran Almog stated the incident aligns with an "evil twin" cyberattack pattern, in which unauthorized access points emulate legitimate networks to attempt credential theft from passengers.
